title: Initial evaluation, right knee, soccer injury

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Hi Jordan. Let's start with the knee. When did it start?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Two months ago during soccer. A pop, then swelling for a week. Pain is 3 out of 10 now, and 7 at the worst.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Giving way twice on pivots. No locking.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any numbness, fever, or pain at night?

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Knee extension is zero degrees today, same as the left. Flexion is 130 degrees on the right and 140 on the left.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Quad strength is 4+/5 on the right with a single-leg test.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I can walk fine and stairs are okay now. Running is still bad.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Next session we'll do a hop test. Right now you're at 60 percent of the left in the single-leg hop.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My goal is to play in the spring season.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Good goal. Assessment: strength is catching up, and the giving way means we keep pivots out for now.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Plan: progress to a slow jog next week only if the swelling stays down. Follow up in one week.

expectedFacts.statement: Pain 3 out of 10 now, 7 at the worst
Giving way twice on pivots, no locking
Single-leg hop at 60 percent of the left
Goal: play in the spring season
Slow jog next week only if swelling stays down
